subject: Bimodal eigenvectors from simple multivariate normal model

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Bimodal eigenvectors from simple multivariate normal model
parts:
I generated some fake 3-variable multivariate data via MASS::mvrnorm, and ran it through the following standard-ish multivariate model:

  data {
    # N: number of cases
    int<lower=1> N ;
    # K: outcomes per case
    int<lower=2> K ;
    # Y: matrix of outcomes for each case & variable
    matrix[N,K] Y ;
  }
  parameters {
    # means: vector of population-level means for intercept & slope
    vector[K] means ;
    # sds: vector of population-level sds for intercept & slope
    vector<lower=0>[K] sds ;
    # cor: population-level correlation between intercept & slope
    corr_matrix[K] cor ;
  }
  transformed parameters{
    # cov: covariance matrix (derived from cor & sds)
    matrix[K,K] cov ; #used in getting correlation to work
    #compute covariance matrix from cor & sds
    cov = quad_form_diag(cor,sds) ;
  }
  model {
    #priors on population parameters; presumes data has been scale()ed
    means ~ normal(0,1) ;
    sds ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    cor ~ lkj_corr(1) ;
    #assert sampling of case-level outcomes on each variable given
    #  multivariate normal population
    for(s in 1:N){
      Y[s,] ~ multi_normal(means,cov) ;
    }
  }

I was interested in doing something akin to principal component analysis, so in R I computed the eigenvectors given each iteration's covariance matrix:

  #get the samples of the covariance matrix
  cov = rstan::extract(post,pars='cov')[[1]]

  #define a function to compute eigenvectors on each sample
  # covariance matrix
  get_evec = function(i){
    e = eigen(cov[i,,])
    v = tibble::as_tibble(eigen(z[i,,])$vectors)
    v$variable = 1:nrow(v)
    v %>% tidyr::gather(
      key = 'component'
      , value = 'value'
      , -variable
    ) 
  }

  #compute all the eigenvectors
  evec = purrr::map_df(
    .x = 1:dim(z)[1]
    , .f = get_evec
  )

  #visualize the eigenvectors
  evec %>%
    ggplot(
      mapping = aes(
        x = value
      )
    )+
    geom_density(
      colour = 'transparent'
      , fill = 'black'
      , alpha = .5
    )+
    facet_wrap(
      ~ component * variable
      , scale = 'free'
      , labeller = labeller(component = label_both,variable=label_both)
    )

Which yields this plot that has clear bimodality in a few of the eigenvectors:

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Bimodal eigenvectors from simple multivariate normal model
parts:
On Wednesday, November 9, 2016 at 8:40:37 PM UTC-5, Mike Lawrence wrote:
Is this expected behaviour? 

Yes. If X * v = lambda * v, you can let w = -v and X * w = lambda * w. If necessary, one way to proceed is to multiply the j-th eigenvector by -1 iff V[1,j] < 0.

Ben

When I do this, I till get a little bit of bimodality ("component: v2; variable: 2" & "component: V2; variable: 3" plots:

I don't think genuine bimodality can be ruled out because the eigenvectors are a complicated function of the covariance matrix. Also, weird numerical things can happen if either the eigenvalues get too close together or too close to zero.
